To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

FM-FM (combination-sensitive) neurons are present in the dorsal and ventral divisions of the mustached bats' medial geniculate bodies (MGB), and that these neurons are tuned to the delay between two harmonics of the bat's biosonar signals (pulse-echo pair).

the MGB contains neurons tuned to the frequency, intensity, and temporal relationship of the FM components in pulse-echo pairs, that these neurons are tuned to small deviations from harmonic relationships in biosonar pulses and Doppler shifted echoes, and that these neurons are relatively tolerant of Doppler-shifted frequency deviations.

FM-FM cells in the medial genicular nucleus of the mustached bats respond to the frequency and intensity of the FM components in the fundamental and second harmonic of the pulse and the second and third harmonic of the echo.

how the auditory system of the mustached bats (Pteronous parnellii) encodes target range information.
the processing of target range information by FM-FM neurons of the mustached bats medial geniculate nucleus (MGB).

FM-FM units in the MGB of mustached bats are combination-sensitive neurons that respond to the combination of the FM component of one of the harmonics of the pulse with one of the FM components from one of the harmonies of the echo.
the combination-sensitive neurons in the M.G.B. of the mustached bats are tuned to the delay between two sounds, and that they are sensitive to the frequency and intensity of each sound in a pair.
the FM-FM neurons of the mustache bat MGB are combination sensitive and delay tuned.

the FM-FM neurons, which we discovered in the mustached bat, are a novel class of neurons in the MGN of the bat that are tuned to combinations of FM sounds.
